content.text:
Both open issues are the release checklists, and [pull request #32](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/pull/32) is already on `main`. The code they describe is in place. The version bumps and the publishes are not.

[#31](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/issues/31) publishes the Go modules at **v0.1.2**. [#28](https://github.com/sandbox-kit/kit/issues/28) publishes the four npm packages at **0.1.4**.

| | Go (#31) | TypeScript (#28) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Current release | `v0.1.1` | `0.1.3` |
| Next release | `v0.1.2` | `0.1.4` |
| Stays put | `internal/sdk` at `v0.1.1` | Daytona `0.225.0`, Modal `0.11.1` |
| Moves | contracts, sandbox, Daytona, Modal | contracts, sandbox, Daytona, Modal |

`internal/sdk` has no changes since its `v0.1.1` tag, so leaving that module alone matches the issue. Contracts did change: `SandboxInfo.origins` and `ValueOrigin` are gone, and field 11 is reserved. Tagging sandbox against contracts `v0.1.1` would put `origins` back on the public Go type, because that type is the generated message.

The `go.mod` and `package.json` files still name the old versions. Examples under `examples/go/` still require `v0.1.1`. Every `replace` line is still there, which is what #31 asks you to keep.

The behavior in both issues matches this tree: the id is read when the call runs, capabilities list the methods the provider implements, close leaves the sandbox running, and TypeScript still has `metadataObjectFromMap` with no size budget.

One line the issues do not mention: the root README still says the TypeScript SDK is published at **0.1.3**. That sentence should say **0.1.4** in the same commit as the package bump.

Yes. `sdks/go/internal/sdk` is the same tree as the `v0.1.1` tag: no commits, and an empty diff. That includes `README.md`, `doc.go`, `error.go`, `unmapped.go`, `duration.go`, `go.mod`, and `go.sum`. The doc edits since that tag do not mention this module.

Its `go.mod` still requires contracts `v0.1.1`. The local `replace` already builds it against the current contracts. Once sandbox `v0.1.2` requires contracts `v0.1.2`, Go selects `v0.1.2` for the whole build, and the existing `internal/sdk` source still compiles against it.
